corrected_label: ABC-type quaternary ammonium compound transporting activity
explanation: The IBD for GO:0005275 amine transmembrane transporter activity at PTN000766131 (PTHR47737, ProW/ChoW-type permeases, about 13 leaf IBAs) is seeded by P. aeruginosa PA5377/CbcW (Q9HTI7, PseudoCAP IDA, PMID:19919675) and E. coli ProW (P14176). Both transport quaternary ammonium compounds (choline, glycine betaine, carnitine, proline betaine), which GO classifies under GO:0015651 and GO:0015418, not under amine transmembrane transporter activity. Please repoint the IBD to GO:0015418 (or GO:0015651). Because the node members are permease subunits, consider contributes_to.

corrected_label: ABC-type quaternary ammonium compound transporting activity
explanation: PA5377 (CbcW permease, Q9HTI7) is annotated GO:0005275 amine transmembrane transporter activity, IDA, PMID:19919675. The substrates shown in that paper (choline, glycine betaine, L-carnitine) are quaternary ammonium compounds, which GO does not class as amines. GO:0015418 ABC-type quaternary ammonium compound transporting activity (with contributes_to for a permease subunit) is the accurate term. This row co-seeds the PAINT IBD at PTN000766131.

The IBD for GO:0015226 carnitine transmembrane transporter activity at PTN000766131 (PTHR47737, about 13 leaf IBAs) rests only on P. aeruginosa PA5377/CbcW (Q9HTI7). In PMID:19919675, carnitine transport by CbcWV requires the separately encoded SBP CaiX (PA5388). The 98-100% identical P. syringae DC3000 Cbc core does not transport carnitine because DC3000 lacks caiX, and E. coli ProW, a co-seed of other IBDs at this node, is not a carnitine transporter. Substrate specificity is therefore not a property of the permease clade. Please remove this IBD, or replace it with GO:0015418 ABC-type quaternary ammonium compound transporting activity (contributes_to).

PA5377 (CbcW, ABC permease) is annotated involved_in GO:0031457 glycine betaine catabolic process (IDA, PMID:19919675). The evidence is that cbc transposon mutants cannot grow on betaine as sole carbon source, which reflects loss of uptake. The permease does not catalyse any catabolic step. Consider removing the row, or keeping only GO:0031460 glycine betaine transport.

PA5377 (CbcW, ABC permease) is annotated involved_in GO:0042426 choline catabolic process (IDA, PMID:19919675 and PMID:21478341). Both papers show that Cbc is needed for growth on choline as a carbon source, which reflects choline uptake. The permease does not perform any catabolic step. GO:0015871 choline transport already captures its role. Consider removing these rows.

The IBD for GO:1902603 carnitine transmembrane transport at PTN000766131 (PTHR47737, about 13 leaf IBAs) rests only on P. aeruginosa PA5377/CbcW (Q9HTI7, PseudoCAP IDA, PMID:21478341). Carnitine uptake by Cbc requires the separately encoded SBP CaiX (PMID:19919675). The 98-100% identical P. syringae DC3000 Cbc core does not transport carnitine, and E. coli ProW, in the same node, is a glycine betaine/proline betaine permease. Carnitine transport is therefore not a clade-wide property of these permeases. Please consider removing the IBD (keeping GO:0031460 and GO:0015871 if desired).

GO:1902603 carnitine transmembrane transport for PA5377 (Q9HTI7) cites PMID:21478341 (Malek et al. 2011), whose abstract deals only with choline uptake by CbcXWV, BetT1 and BetT3. The carnitine evidence for CbcWV is in PMID:19919675 (PA14 cbc mutants fail to grow on carnitine, and PAO1 CbcWV restores CaiX-dependent carnitine uptake) and PMID:29517479. If PMID:21478341 has no carnitine data, please re-key the row. It is the sole seed of the PAINT IBD at PTN000766131.
